lyon_arboretum: Is an public arboretum and botanical garden
Located in the upper end of Manoa Valley in Oahu
The Lyon Arboretum is the only university-owned botanical garden in the United States. Which is managed by the University of Hawaii at Manoa.
Has more than 6,000 tropical and subtropical plants across its 193.5 acres.
Has over 7 miles of hiking trials
Waiahole_Beach_Park: Located on the windward coast of Oahu along Kaneohe Bay.
Swimming in the beach park isn't possible due to the ocean bottom being shallow and has a reef.
Mokoli'i Island can be seen in the distance
Can view Ko'olau Mountains and Kaneohe Bay
The park is popular for fishing, picnics, short walks, and bay views.
Kapolei: As of 2026, Kapolei has a population of 24,844 people.
Kapolei is known as Oahu's 'second city'.
The name 'Kapolei' originates from 'Pu'u o Kapolei'. Pu'u meaning 'hill' and Kapo lei meaning 'beloved Kapo' (Kapo was a sister of Pele)
Kapolei High School is the first traditional high school to open in July of 2000. The last high school that opened in Oahu was Kaiser High in 1971. (located in Hawaii Kai)
In 1879, Kapolei was used as sugarcane and pineapple plantations by an industrialist named James Campbell.
